in_code_these_turn:
In code these turn into ordinary habits rather than slogans. Simplicity is KISS and YAGNI:
        build the straightforward thing that is actually needed, and leave out the abstraction that
        might be needed one day. Purpose is what stops a feature from existing only because it was
        possible. Balance is where DRY lives — shared design tokens and small focused functions,
        while leaving harmless duplication alone when removing it would hurt readability. Continuous
        improvement is where SOLID and GRASP earn their place: one clear responsibility per function,
        each one handed only the data it needs, so the next change stays cheap. This site is built
        that way too.
